name: Nadab
overview: Nadab, the son of Aaron, is introduced in Scripture as one of the priests set apart to minister before the Lord, called alongside Moses, Aaron, and the elders of Israel to worship at Mount Sinai (Exodus 24:1, 9). He is explicitly named among Aaron's sons consecrated for the priestly office, highlighting his role in the sacred service (Exodus 6:23; 28:1). The detailed description of the holy garments made for Aaron and his sons underscores the solemnity and divine appointment of Nadab's priestly duties (Exodus 28:4). These passages collectively emphasize Nadab's privileged position in Israel's worship and the seriousness of the priesthood to which he was called.
